title: Effectiveness of an Echinacea toothpaste in relation to biofilm and gingivitis - a clinical study
summary: Optimal oral hygiene includes the daily removal of bacterial plaque, which can be mastered with the help of a toothbrush and the correct toothpaste. Apart from the removal of plaque, the choice of the right toothpaste can depend on the individual needs of the patient. Patients who have periodontitis or frequent bleeding gums will be able to achieve more effective results with toothpastes specialized for these issues than with conventional toothpastes. A simple and home-based method to combat bleeding gums could be the use of Paromed toothpaste from Mara expert®. This toothpaste promises to be effective against bleeding gums and "periodontal disease". Whether and to what extent this toothpaste can be used to counteract gum problems will be investigated as part of an eight-week clinical trial. 80 participants (40 women, 40 men) aged between 18 and 65 will take part in the study. The participants will all receive the same materials: a bag with the study information, a toothbrush, toothpaste, toothpicks and a questionnaire. One half receives a toothpaste whose ingredients are particularly effective against bleeding gums and periodontal disease and can therefore reduce the degree of inflammation in the gums. The other group receives a conventional toothpaste without special anti-bleeding and anti-inflammatory properties. The oral hygiene quality of the participants is examined in an initial, intermediate and final examination, in which the same parameters are recorded in each case. The number of plaque deposits and whether or how much the gums bleed are measured. In the final examination, a questionnaire is completed by each participant. The study is evaluated anonymously. All data protection rules will be observed. It is assumed that an echinacea toothpaste can reduce the degree of bleeding of the gums more effectively than the comparison toothpaste.

interventions.name: 40 partially randomized  (stratified according to gender and age) assigned subjects use the test toothpaste, in a period of 8 weeks (2 minutes twice a day).
40 partially randomized  (stratified according to gender and age) assigned subjects use the control toothpaste (placebo), in a period of 8 weeks (2 minutes twice a day)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- At least 16 uncrowned teeth
- Papilla bleeding index ≥ 0.5
- Quigley-Hein index (modified according to Turesky) ≥ 2
- Existing informed consent for participation in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding or planning a pregnancy during the study period
- Uncontrolled diabetes (type I and II)
- Existing removable dentures  
- Fixed or removable orthodontic appliance
- Aggressive or severe chronic periodontitis
- Previous participation in the study
- Participation in another clinical study or use of another product to be tested within the last 30 days before the first examination
- Use of antibiotics within the last 14 days before the first examination or other medication or the presence of a therapy that could influence the study results.
- Known or suspected allergy to one or more ingredients of the toothpaste
- Alcohol or drug abuse within one year before the start of the first examination
